tasks.description: Extend the pure task model and persistence boundary in src/tasks.js with priority values High, Medium, and Low. New tasks default to Medium; legacy saved tasks missing priority load as Medium without erasing or rewriting storage. Reject unknown stored or input values. Keep updateTask immutable and preserve priority on unrelated changes. Add a pure sortTasks function ordered by High, Medium, Low, then ascending createdAt, then lexical task ID, without mutating the input array. Add deterministic model tests.
acceptance_criteria: createTask defaults priority to Medium and accepts only High, Medium, or Low; updateTask preserves it unless changes explicitly include priority.
parseTasks and loadTasks normalize legacy records missing priority to Medium; invalid stored priority is reported while saved storage remains unchanged.
sortTasks returns a new array ordered High, Medium, Low, then earlier createdAt, then lexical task ID; it does not mutate the input.
Tests cover defaults, legacy loading, invalid values, all priority levels, creation-order ties, ID ties, and immutability.

tasks.description: Add labeled priority selects to both create and edit forms in index.html. Wire src/app.js so create passes the selected priority to createTask, edit preloads the current priority and passes changes to updateTask, and successful changes use the existing persistence and render path. Show a visible priority label on each card with textContent; adjust styles.css only as needed. Preserve priority when status changes and show model validation errors without losing saved tasks.
acceptance_criteria: Create and edit forms offer Low, Medium, and High with Medium selected by default for new tasks; edit preloads the task's current value.
Creating or editing priority saves the selected value and immediately rerenders the board; a status-only change retains priority.
Every card displays its priority using textContent; no user-provided text is inserted with innerHTML.
Invalid priority is rejected through the model and reported by the existing status message without overwriting localStorage.

tasks.description: Update src/app.js rendering to call the pure sortTasks function for the visible tasks in each status column. Keep tasks in their status columns and retain existing task controls. Sorting must take effect immediately after priority edits and status moves. Complete any necessary deterministic model tests in tests/tasks.test.js and run all allowlisted validation commands.
acceptance_criteria: Within each status column, cards render High before Medium before Low, with earlier createdAt first and task ID breaking exact timestamp ties.
Changing priority immediately reorders the current column; moving a task retains its priority and places it correctly in the destination column.
The underlying task array and saved data are not reordered merely by rendering.
npm test, node --check src/app.js, and node --check src/tasks.js all pass.
